# MM-P2-L1-IH02 Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #2

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Scope
- This manual defines required maintenance activities, inspection rationale, and acceptance criteria for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2, equipment id EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Applies to mechanical, electrical, and cooling subsystems that directly affect billet heating performance and operator safety.
- Related change documents and procedures: ECN-2026-013, ECN-2026-039, SOP-P2-L1-01.

Background and purpose
- EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is an induction billet heater used to prepare billets for hot forging operations on line P2-L1. Proper maintenance ensures consistent heating profile, coil integrity, and cooling system reliability.
- The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C. Achieving and holding this target requires verified coil geometry, correct power delivery, and adequate coil cooling.
- The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Maintaining at-or-above this flow prevents coil overheating and rapid insulation degradation.
- This manual focuses on preventive measures and acceptance checks that mitigate unplanned downtime and extend component life.

Tools
- Standard electrical troubleshooting kit capable of verifying continuity and insulation resistance.
- Pressure-rated hose and fittings compatible with the plant cooling water supply and hose connection hardware on EQ-P2-L1-IH02.
- Thermal imaging device for surface temperature mapping and verification of uniform heat distribution across the billet path.
- Non-destructive inspection tools for coil and busbar inspection (visual magnifier, borescope).
- Torque tools and calibration certificates are maintained per plant calibration control. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-01 for tool control and calibration traceability.

Procedure
- General approach: Perform visual and functional inspections, verify cooling flow, and map heating performance. Record observations in the equipment maintenance log and attach supporting data from thermal imaging and flow verification.
- Pre-maintenance safety: Isolate EQ-P2-L1-IH02 from power and lockout per SOP-P2-L1-01. Verify cooling water valves are in the safe position and draining is complete before accessing coil assemblies. Confirm with the shift supervisor before proceeding.
- Coil and busbar inspection: Visually inspect coil windings for signs of insulation cracking, coolant leakage, or displacement. Use borescope to inspect internal turns where accessible. Inspect busbar connections for discoloration or loose connectors. Clean external surfaces with compatible solvents and lint-free cloths as required.
- Cooling system verification: Connect a calibrated flow indicator to the coil supply line and verify the coil cooling water flow is at or above 55 L/min. If flow is below the minimum, do not operate the heater. Trace and repair restricted sections in the supply line, verify inlet and outlet valves, and remove any inline strainers for inspection and cleaning. Record pre- and post-repair flow values in the maintenance log.
- Electrical checks: With power isolated, perform insulation resistance tests on coil windings per plant electrical standards. Verify continuity and absence of short circuits before reapplying power. Inspect power feed connectors and contactors for wear; replace per vendor guidance if degradation is evident.
- Functional heat mapping: After completing mechanical and electrical checks and restoring normal coolant flow, restore power and perform a controlled heat validation using a test billet or calibrated thermal simulator. Use thermal imaging device to map temperature uniformity across the billet path and verify the billet reaches the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C at the specified measurement point. Document the thermal map and any deviations.
- Corrective actions and examples: If thermal mapping shows a cold zone near a specific coil segment, inspect that coil segment for turn-to-turn shorts, insulation breakdown, or coolant obstructions. Example corrective actions include reseating coil clamps, repairing coolant channels, or replacing damaged coil segments. If repeated heating shortfalls occur after corrective action, escalate to engineering and reference ECN-2026-013 and ECN-2026-039 for previous change history and modifications that may affect coil transfer function.
- Post-maintenance steps: Update the equipment maintenance log with serial identifiers of replaced components, test results from insulation checks, coolant flow verification entries, and attached thermal maps. Notify operations that the heater is returned to service and include any operational limits or observations that operators should monitor during the initial production period.

Records to keep
- Equipment maintenance log entry for each maintenance event, including technician name, date, and summaries of inspections and tests.
- Thermal imaging files and annotated maps showing temperature distribution and indicating the location where the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C was measured.
- Cooling flow verification records showing measured flow at coil supply before and after any corrective action, confirming coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min is met.
- Insulation resistance and continuity test reports with pass/fail status and measured values.
- Parts replaced and disposition records, and any escalation records referencing ECN-2026-013 or ECN-2026-039.

Acceptance criteria
- Mechanical: Coil windings show no visible insulation failure or coolant leakage; busbar connectors are secure and free of overheating indicators.
- Cooling: Measured coil cooling water flow meets or exceeds 55 L/min. If flow is below this minimum, the heater must remain offline until flow is restored and verified.
- Electrical: Insulation resistance and continuity tests meet plant electrical acceptance thresholds per SOP-P2-L1-01. No shorts or grounding faults present.
- Thermal performance: Billet temperature mapping demonstrates that the billet reaches the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 1180 °C within the defined billet travel path and exhibits acceptable uniformity. Any deviation that could affect forging outcomes must be corrected and retested before return to production.
- Documentation: All required records are filed in the equipment maintenance folder and cross-referenced to SOP-P2-L1-01 and change documents ECN-2026-013 and ECN-2026-039 as applicable.

Notes and rationale
- Verifying cooling flow is prioritized because inadequate flow accelerates coil damage and leads to rapid failure modes that are more costly and hazardous.
- Thermal mapping provides direct evidence that electrical power and mechanical coil geometry produce the expected billet heating outcome; it is the final acceptance check prior to returning EQ-P2-L1-IH02 to production.
- Use the related documents ECN-2026-013 and ECN-2026-039 for historical modification details and SOP-P2-L1-01 for lockout/tagout and tool calibration governance.
